rationale_overall: Filtered out a large volume of non-investable noise: foreign government/military items (Indian and Pakistani nuclear/satellite programs, North Korea missile tests, Kursk plant drone strike, Taiwan referendum, India-HAL/GE talks), private-company coverage with no public ticker (SpaceX Starship test-flight cycle, FieldAI funding round), and generic 'top AI stocks to buy' listicles that name no fresh catalyst for names not already held. The two candidates with a real US-listed ticker attached — Rocket Lab (RKLB, rockets_spacecraft wave) and Uranium Royalty Corp (nuclear wave) — were each weak: RKLB's coverage this week is a stock-down-today piece plus speculative price-target chatter, not a commercial milestone, and Uranium Royalty's news is a routine at-the-market equity program (dilutive housekeeping, plus thin/TSX-primary liquidity), not a buildup catalyst. Nvidia's H20/China chip-curb story touches an existing holding (NVDA) but is regulatory friction, not a thesis breach, so it doesn't warrant a remove. No candidate cleared the bar of a genuine rising-wave catalyst strong enough to justify swapping out AAPL, GOOGL, MSFT, or NVDA under the paired add/remove constraint, so the watchlist is unchanged this week.
